paper.title: Continuous opinions and discrete actions in opinion dynamics problems

headline: Martins 2008 CODA (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; hidden beliefs extremize to max|l|/nu~1756 (still doubling), final extremist-dominated, same-action clusters collapse ~337->8 (bar 250); distinctness signature: discrete-action Bayesian updating DIVERGES to certainty, inverting bounded-confidence averaging

verdicts.gate: P1 opinions extremize without bound: max|l|/nu >= 100 at 2M updates AND still growing (>= 1.3x when doubled to 4M)
P2 final distribution is U-shaped / extremist-dominated: frac(|l|/nu >= 50) > frac(|l|/nu < 1) at the end of the run
P3 agreeing agents form contiguous same-action domains: connected same-action clusters <= 0.1*N (far below the random start)

extra.framing: genuine agent-based — each agent carries a hidden continuous log-odds belief and exposes only a discrete action; the unit of action is one asynchronous single-observation Bayesian update
extra.distinctness: discrete-action Bayesian updating DIVERGES to certainty (extremization); inverts bounded-confidence (Deffuant/HK) averaging toward moderation
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + lock-first discipline reproduce extremization + same-action domain formation and would catch an artifact

citations: Martins, A.C.R. (2008). Continuous opinions and discrete actions in opinion dynamics problems. Int. J. Mod. Phys. C 19(4):617-624. doi:10.1142/S0129183108012339. (arXiv:0711.1199.)

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the locked extremization, bimodality, and same-action domain-count metrics
